text:
emma: hey team, day 1 finished but i'm hitting repeat trouble. i need to talk to our internal docker registry (registry.int.redwood) during builds, but split-tunnel DNS/route doesn't let my laptop reach it. ssh tunnel worked once (thanks mir a), but i keep forgetting to start it. any tips to make the tunnel persistent across reboots?

mira: welcome emma! two quick approaches: 1) make an ssh config + a small background command, or 2) use autossh/systemd/launchd to keep the tunnel alive. which OS?

emma: macbook m2, macos 13.6. prefer something low-friction.

alex: on mac i use a small launchd plist to run autossh at login. autossh reconnects automatically if the tunnel drops. example plist (save to ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.redwood.tunnel.plist):

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
  <dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>com.redwood.tunnel</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
      <string>/usr/local/bin/autossh</string>
      <string>-M</string>
      <string>0</string>
      <string>-f</string>
      <string>-N</string>
      <string>-L</string>
      <string>5000:10.7.2.10:5000</string>
      <string>ubuntu@bastion.redwood</string>
    </array>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
  </dict>
</plist>
```

alex: then `launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.redwood.tunnel.plist` and it's persistent. autossh binary can be installed via homebrew.

emma: nice. will that keep it from using tons of battery? i've seen background ssh hang sometimes.

mira: autossh keeps a minimal connection; `-M 0` disables monitoring port (useful on mac) but restart behavior still works. if you want low-power, use `ServerAliveInterval 60` in your ssh config and use a background `ssh -fN` instead of autossh.

emma: any caveats for docker builds that need the registry? i run `docker build` locally, and it fails unless i `npm login` inside the Dockerfile step.

alex: two things: 1) route the daemon traffic through the host proxy by building with `--network=host` on Linux hosts (not supported on mac docker for mac), or 2) use `docker buildx` with an auth helper and pass `--secret` or `--build-arg` for credentials. many folks wrap builds by making the registry accessible at localhost:5000 via the tunnel and then use `docker build --build-arg REGISTRY=localhost:5000` so the build can pull.

emma: i'm on Docker Desktop on mac, so network=host not available. will try the localhost:5000 approach.

mira: also note TLS: if the registry uses internal certs, point docker to the tunneled host by adding an insecure-registries entry in Docker daemon config (only for dev machines) or install the internal CA into macOS and Docker cert store. both have onboarding/security implications.

it-bot: created ticket #7218: "Provide documented autossh/launchd example for new hires + guidance on Docker Desktop workflows" assigned to @mira.

netops-bot: quick FYI: we're working on improving split-DNS and resolver push. long term we'll provide a VPN profile that includes internal resolver IP and common service domains for new hires. ETA 2 business days for a staged rollout.

emma: thanks all, i'll test the launchd plist. could we add a short note in the new-hire VPN doc describing: autossh example (mac), systemd unit (linux), `ssh -D` socks option (for browser auth), and the docker localhost pattern? i nearly wasted half a day figuring out auth in builds.

mira: good call. i'll add a compact how-to to the onboarding checklist and link the ticket. welcome again :)

emma: super helpful, appreciate it :thumbsup:
